evals.prompt: Morning note for the coverage list. Overnight news on Northwind Robotics is attached. What is our take, and do we change the rating?
assertions: Opens with a Top Call headline that gives a view on Northwind, not only a summary of the news
Uses the morning-note sections (Top Call, Overnight or Pre-Market Developments, Key Events Today, Trade Ideas) and stays on one page max, readable in 2 minutes
States the rating decision (maintain, upgrade or downgrade) and the price target, with one sentence of reason

evals.prompt: Keep it short: only the Northwind take for today's meeting, nothing on the sector.
assertions: Covers Northwind only and leaves out the sector pre-announcement item
Still states a top call and a rating decision

evals.prompt: Give me a trade idea on Northwind off the supplier news, with the catalyst and what would make it wrong.
assertions: Trade Ideas gives a long or short call with a one-to-two sentence thesis and names the catalyst
States the risk: what would make the trade wrong
Sizes the Q4 revenue at risk from the supplier delay against Q4 consensus of $428.0M (consensus as of 2026-10-20)

evals.prompt: What in the overnight news is noise, and what matters for the morning meeting on Northwind?
assertions: Treats the supplier shipment delay as actionable and the trade-association order statistic as noise
Says plainly when an item does not change the thesis, rather than padding the note
Notes that the take is pre-market and may change by the open

evals.prompt: Quick takes on Northwind's Q3 print for the morning meeting: consensus against actual, then our action.
assertions: Quick-takes table with Metric, Consensus, Actual and Beat/Miss columns for revenue ($405.0M and $412.0M), EPS ($0.79 and $0.84) and gross margin (40.8% and 41.5%)
Gives an Our Take of two to three sentences on whether the print changes the thesis
Gives an Action line: maintain, upgrade or downgrade, and any price target change

evals.prompt: Need to get ready for the 7am meeting. Two of my semis names reported after the close last night, and futures are down 1%. Can you draft something tight for the PMs?
what happened overnight across my consumer staples coverage? I want a quick writeup with our view on each before the open
Write today's daily note for the energy desk. Brent is up 3% on the OPEC headlines, and XOM has its investor day at 10am.
Morning call prep: Nike beat on EPS but cut its FY guide. I need a 2-minute read with a top call, a quick beat/miss table, and whether we stay at Buy.
Nothing really happened overnight in my REIT coverage. Can you still put together a short note for the morning meeting that says we're holding positioning?
Pre-market: there's a rumor that Pfizer is bidding for one of my mid-cap biotech names, which is up 25%. Draft a Slack-ready blurb for the traders with our take and a long/short idea.
Put together this morning's note for the banks team. CPI is out at 8:30, JPM was downgraded by a competitor, and the 10y is up 8bps overnight. Keep it to one page.
Yesterday I said to buy AMD into the print and I was wrong. Draft today's 7am note so it owns that call and gives the updated view.
Microsoft reports next Tuesday. Build me a preview of what consensus expects and the key metrics to watch on the call.
Do a full post-earnings deep dive on Salesforce's Q3. Segment trends, margin bridge, and the implications for our long-term estimates.
Map out every catalyst for my healthcare coverage over the next quarter: FDA dates, conferences, and earnings.
Screen the industrials space for new long ideas based on valuation and estimate revisions. I'm looking for fresh names to pitch.
Can you write a birthday message for my coworker who loves hiking?
Explain how to set up a Python virtual environment on Windows.
Give me a 20-minute morning workout I can do without equipment.
